title: Leaves come in many shapes

body.heading: Round, long and wiggly
paragraphs: Walk around a garden or a park and look at the leaves. This leaf is round. That leaf is long and thin. Here is a leaf shaped like a heart!
Leaves are not all the same green, either. Some are dark green, some are light green, and some are soft and fuzzy to touch — touch gently, with one finger.

body.heading: Count the shapes
paragraphs: How many leaf shapes can you find? One, two, three, more? Point at each new shape and say what it looks like: a coin, a ribbon, a star, a hand.
You can draw your favourite leaf when you get home. Draw its shape first. Then colour it the right green.

takeaway: Leaves come in many shapes — round, long, wiggly and heart-shaped — and spotting them is a game anyone can play.
ageGuidance: Ages 3-8: read aloud with a grown-up, ideally before a walk.
materials: This is a reading item — no materials needed
supervision: Read together with a grown-up; leaf-spotting outdoors must be with a grown-up.
safetyNotes: Look at leaves without picking them from other people's gardens.
Do not eat any leaves or berries — some can make you poorly. Wash hands after touching plants.
screenFreeExtension: On your next walk, find one leaf shaped like a heart and one shaped like a star.
